contents.text: <instructions>Read "Grasshopper and the Ants," a fable by Aesop.</instructions>

elements.text: It was summer. The air was warm, the grass was green, and there was plenty of food. Every day, Grasshopper slept in the sun, played in the grass, and filled his belly.
One day, some little ants walked by with heavy loads on their backs. Grasshopper asked them what they were doing. One ant told Grasshopper that they were storing food for winter.
"But it's summer now," said Grasshopper. "There is plenty of food."
The ants simply went back to work. Grasshopper chewed on some grass. Then, he took a nap.

That winter, the air grew cold. The grass turned gray. There was no food around, and Grasshopper hadn't stored any. The ants had stored plenty of food. So, they got to eat while Grasshopper was weak and hungry. Grasshopper wished he had worked more during the summer!

contents.text: <instructions>When winter came, why was Grasshopper weak and hungry?</instructions>

choices.text: He had not stored food for winter.
He had been working too hard.

<instructions>Read "The Poor Man and the Honey," a folktale from India.</instructions>

elements.text: One day, a poor farmer found a big jar of honey. Excited, he placed it on the top shelf in his kitchen.

That night, the farmer wondered about the jar of honey. "If I sold it, I bet I could buy five sheep. And every year, the sheep would have babies. I would have many lambs. After the lambs grew up, I could sell all of my animals. I would be rich! I would have a wife. And we would have a son! Oh, he would be such a fine boy!"

Lost in his daydream, the farmer swung his arms in excitement. He knocked the honey jar off the shelf. The jar fell on the floor, and the honey was spilled. Now the man had no honey and his dreams were lost.

<instructions>Read "Mr. Rat Looks for a Wife," a Japanese fable.</instructions>

elements.text: Mr. Rat loved Ms. Rat, and she loved him, too. But Mr. Rat wouldn't marry her. He wanted to marry the strongest thing in the world.
He thought the Sun was the strongest, so he asked her first. The Sun said, "But the Cloud is stronger than I, for she blocks my light."
So, Mr. Rat went to the Cloud. The Cloud said, "But the Wind is stronger than I, for she pushes me around."
So, Mr. Rat went to the Wind next. The Wind said, "But the Wall is stronger than I. No matter how strong I blow, she always stands."
So, Mr. Rat went to the Wall. The Wall said, "But there is one thing stronger than I. She can chew holes in me. You have known her all your life, and you are already in love with her."

Then, the oldest mouse got up to speak. "All right," he said. "But who will be the one to tie the bell on that cat?"
The mice just looked at one another. Nobody spoke up. They all thought it was a smart idea, but everyone was too scared to actually do it!

This story made the king turn red with anger. So, he let the horse live in the royal stable. And he made the knight live in the stable with the horse, too. Then, he ordered the knight to take good care of his horse.

elements.text: A father and his son were walking into town with their donkey. Someone passed them and said, "Why walk? You can ride that donkey, you know!" So, the father let his son ride, and they walked on.

Soon, another man passed them. "What a lazy boy!" he complained. "He should walk and let his poor old father ride." The father liked that idea. He ordered his son off the donkey and got on it himself.
Later, a woman passed them. "What kind of father makes his son walk?" she asked. Hearing this, the father let his son ride with him.
Later, a traveler passed them. "Shame on you!" he cried. "That poor donkey is too small to carry you both!"
"Fine! You take the donkey," the father huffed. He handed the reins to the traveler. "Now are you happy?"
The father was angry. He had tried to make everyone happy. But no matter what he did, someone was always mad at him.

elements.text: A poor man came to a town. The townspeople only had a little bit of food, so they could not offer him a meal. "Then I will make stone soup!" the man said. He pulled a stone out of his pocket. Then, he filled a large pot with water, lit a fire under it, and dropped in the stone.

The townspeople wondered how someone could make soup with a stone. The man stirred the pot and said, "Mmmm, delicious. I only wish I had some carrots." Before long, someone found some carrots and added them to the pot.
"Perfect!" the man said. "Now, if only I had some potatoes." Hearing this, someone found some potatoes and added them to the pot.
"Wonderful!" said the man. "Now, if only I had some chicken, this soup would please a king." Then, someone found some chicken and added it to the pot.
After other people added what they could, there was tasty soup for all!

elements.text: Nino was a messy kid. His clothes were always stained and dirty.

elements.text: Fox was always playing tricks on Stork. But Stork was happy when Fox asked her over for dinner anyway.

Fox made soup for dinner. He set two hot bowls on the table. The soup smelled good, and Stork was hungry. But her soup bowl was wide and not very deep. With her long bill, she could hardly eat a drop.
Fox had played another trick on her!
